questions.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
questions.problem:
Consider a system of $n$ linear equations in $n$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,z=c.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $z$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $c$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & =\bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{{D}^{-1}}}}c \\ \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{{I}_{n}}}}z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and right to left, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
questions.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,z=c$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,z & =c \\ {D}^{-1}D\,z & ={D}^{-1}c \\ {I}_{n}\,z & ={D}^{-1}\,c \\ z & ={D}^{-1}\,c\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and ${I}_{n}.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and ${I}_{n}.$

questions.problem:
Consider a system of $n$ linear equations in $n$ variables, written in matrix form as $D\,t=q.$ Here, $D$ is the non-singular coefficient matrix of the system, $t$ is the column vector containing the variables, and $q$ is the column vector containing the constants. The unique solution of the system can be found using the method shown below:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,t & =q \\ \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{{D}^{-1}}}}D\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ {I}_{n}\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,\bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\color{blue}{\phantom{\mathbf{q}}}} \\ t & ={D}^{-1}\,q\end{aligned}
$$

From top to bottom and left to right, what are the missing parts of the derivation?
questions.worked_solution:
Since $D$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${D}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $D\,t=q$ by ${D}^{-1},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}D\,t & =q \\ {D}^{-1}D\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ {I}_{n}\,t & ={D}^{-1}\,q \\ t & ={D}^{-1}\,q\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing parts are ${D}^{-1}$ and $q.$
